newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Gold prices were mixed on Istanbul's gold exchange in quiet trade due to holiday in the U.S. markets, dealers said.
Gold closed at $388.00 an ounce, down $1.10 from Thursday, but up 1,950 lira at 1,082,500 lira per gram due to a weaker lira. Turkish markets were closed for a holiday on Friday.
Volume rose to 1,150 kilos from Thursday's 849, mainly due to registry deals in the morning session, dealers said.
Exchange members have to register imported gold on the bourse by selling and buying by themselves before selling it to second parties on the free market.

"Seasonal demand from the free market continues but the bulk of the morning deals was made in lira terms to register imports. Sellers shied away from direct sales because they thought the lira was not weak enough," said one free market dealer.
Of the total 855 kilos of morning trade, 650 were in lira terms. But 285 of the 295 kilos traded in the afternoon were in dollar terms.
Members prefer to sell imported gold in lira terms to make a profit when the lira weakens significantly versus the dollar. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
